title: Frontend engineer
summary: Builds the part of a product people see and touch: interfaces that are fast, accessible and work on every screen.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: The web platform every framework sits on.

stages.title: Core stack
stages.caption: A typed language, a component framework and how state flows through it.

stages.title: Tooling and quality
stages.caption: Build, test and ship with confidence.

stages.title: Going further
stages.caption: What separates senior frontend work: rendering strategy, performance and design systems.

title: Backend engineer
summary: Builds the services, APIs and data layer behind a product, and keeps them correct and reliable under load.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: One server language well, and how the web talks.

stages.title: Core stack
stages.caption: A framework, a database and the habits that keep data consistent.

stages.title: Shipping it
stages.caption: Package, test and deploy your service.

stages.title: Going further
stages.caption: Systems that span many machines and many teams.

title: Full-stack engineer
summary: Owns a feature end to end, from the database to the button, usually in one language across both sides.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: The web platform plus one language for both sides.

stages.title: Core stack
stages.caption: One framework that covers UI and server, plus a database and auth.

stages.title: Shipping it
stages.caption: Test, deploy and watch what you ship.

stages.title: Going further
stages.caption: The trade-offs you own when you own the whole feature.

title: Mobile developer
summary: Builds apps for phones and tablets, native or cross-platform, that feel fast and work offline.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: A mobile language and how apps live on a device.

stages.title: Native UI
stages.caption: The declarative UI toolkits on each platform.

stages.title: Cross-platform
stages.caption: One codebase for both stores.

stages.title: Going further
stages.caption: The services and polish real apps need.

title: DevOps / platform engineer
summary: Builds the paths code takes to production and keeps the systems it runs on healthy, repeatable and observable.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: The operating system, networks and a scripting language.

stages.title: Containers and delivery
stages.caption: Package everything the same way and ship it automatically.

stages.title: Infrastructure
stages.caption: Clusters and clouds, described as code.

stages.title: Reliability
stages.caption: Know when things break, and break less.

title: Data engineer
summary: Moves, cleans and models data so analysts and models can trust it, in batch and in real time.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: SQL, a data language and how databases store things.

stages.title: Pipelines
stages.caption: Extract, transform, load, on a schedule.

stages.title: Warehouses and lakes
stages.caption: Where analytics data lives at scale.

stages.title: Going further
stages.caption: Streaming and the modern lakehouse.

title: Machine learning engineer
summary: Trains, evaluates and serves models, and turns research results into reliable product features.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: The maths and the Python stack underneath every model.

stages.title: Classical ML
stages.caption: Learning from labelled data, and knowing when it's working.

stages.title: Deep learning
stages.caption: Neural networks and the frameworks that train them.

stages.title: Production
stages.caption: From notebook to a model people depend on.

title: AI application engineer
summary: Builds products on top of large language models: retrieval, agents, evaluation and guardrails.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: How LLMs work, at the level an app builder needs.

stages.title: Retrieval
stages.caption: Give the model the right context.

stages.title: Agents and tools
stages.caption: Let the model act, safely.

stages.title: Going further
stages.caption: Measure quality and keep it safe.

title: Security engineer
summary: Finds and fixes weaknesses before attackers do, and builds systems that stay safe when something fails.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: Networks, operating systems and the basics of cryptography.

stages.title: Identity and access
stages.caption: Who are you, and what may you do?

stages.title: Application security
stages.caption: The bugs that show up again and again.

stages.title: Offense and response
stages.caption: Think like an attacker, respond like a defender.

title: Game developer
summary: Builds interactive worlds: gameplay code, rendering, physics and the tools artists use.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: A performance-minded language and the maths of space.

stages.title: Engines
stages.caption: Where most games are built today.

stages.title: Graphics
stages.caption: How a frame gets drawn.

stages.title: Going further
stages.caption: Worlds that generate themselves, and new platforms.

title: Embedded engineer
summary: Writes the software inside devices, close to the hardware, where memory and timing are tight.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: C, memory and how a computer actually runs code.

stages.title: Microcontrollers
stages.caption: Talking to hardware directly.

stages.title: Real-time systems
stages.caption: Deadlines that must never be missed.

stages.title: Going further
stages.caption: Connected devices and Linux on the edge.
